card.name: Linking words before antiemetic premedication drugs
card.fires_on: Commas, 'and', 'with', 'including' and 'administer' right before a listed premedication drug, such as antiemetics, antihistamines, corticosteroids or serotonin antagonists. Seen in oncology dosing sections on nausea and infusion-reaction prevention.

modes.label: Link before premedication drug
modes.description: A comma or small linking word sits between premedication drugs in a list or just before the next one.
modes.example: safely administered with corticosteroids<<,>> analgesics, antiemetics /

modes.label: Administer before premedication
modes.description: The verb 'administer' or its article comes just before an antihistamine or corticosteroid to be given beforehand.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words like 'growth', which is an odd fit, so the output effect is unclear.
card.plain: It fires on the small words that lead into the next pre-treatment drug, like an anti-nausea medicine or steroid.
